NOOWW you say they're mutually exclusive! I knew it!

Ah. That complicates things. If "educated" here refers only to formal education, I'll go with my original answer. If it refers to every type of learning, including what I normally get from books, I'll have to go with well educated. One can be satisfied and content without ever being happy, which is a pretty generic term anyway.

So, I think I figured this question out. It seemed tough at first. And I think it is one of those questions that everyone asks of themselves at some point. Once I realized that this is a question that has been posed a number of different times in my life, the question became pretty clear. You can frame it in a lot of different ways, and I think the "red pill / blue pill" question kind of touched on this a little bit.

Interestingly, I feel that I know one of these positions quite well, if we are assuming that these states of being are exclusive of one another. I feel that I am a pretty well-educated person. I think, objectively, most people would say, "yes, you are well educated." I hold a Master's degree, and I had a professor once tell me that this would place me in the top 4% of the population in terms of education. (Note: I have no idea if this is true or not. It's just what I was told. Take that for what you will.) Simultaneously, I have suffered from lifelong depression. It's common in my family. So, the happy-uneducated position is the foreign territory for me.

Still, though, I think I've been settled on this for quite some time. Succinctly: "ignorance is bliss." Or, have I?

This is rather interesting. Because education is something I value so much. It is a noble endeavor, and the more educated the population is, the better our society will be. But, let's put happiness on the hot seat for a moment. Is happiness contagious? Or is happiness a zero-sum game? Is our society also increasingly better if more people are happy? When you smile at someone, they are more likely to smile back, right? Because we naturally mimic these nonverbal gestures, right? So, does happiness function similarly? Or is it so that if one person is happy, this person has legitimate reasons to be. You can only be happy if unhappiness also exists, right? Happiness is relative, right? We can look at this in two ways: happiness can only be experienced if one is also experiencing unhappiness. Or, alternatively, if you are happy, you must have gotten the better end of the deal, and someone else is experiencing unhappiness at the same level of happiness that you are experiencing. The better your life is going to be, the worse someone else's life is going to be, because happiness is relative. So, is happiness really the "end-all-be-all" state of being that it seems to be at the superficial level? Or not? Is it this massive castle in the sky? Humanity's greatest illusion? I don't know.

But back to education. Now, this is really interesting. Because education is a social construction. It exists as its own pursuit. Those who are educated have put in the legwork to discover and explore. An education is an acquisition of knowledge. To not be educated implies that you would be ignorant. So, these are your options. However, you can be either educated or ignorant, and still be intelligent. This is really important. Because if you choose to be ignorant/uneducated, you have the possibility of being an intelligent person. Not guaranteed, but it's possible. This is a definite plus in this column.

Now that I'm sort of looking at the options of sad-educated and happy-ignorant, I cannot help but observe that, most likely, ignorance is often harmful to other people. You lack a general understanding of other people, other cultures, other ways of living. And so the zero-sum game of happiness really does exist. Is it worth it to be happy, while others are unhappy? Or is it better to be sad, knowing that you are contributing to a greater amount of happiness among other people? If we are all choosing to be educated, do we balance everything out, sacrificing some level of happiness in hopes of elevating from the unhappiness of the general population? If personal happiness can only exist alongside personal unhappiness, then isn't this our only real option? To be educated, and try to balance it out to a healthy average among everyone? I think so. Right?
